rationale: This record comprises extended abstracts from a biomedical microbiology and nutrition symposium focusing on infant gut microbiota maturation, enteric pathogen carriage, breastfeeding, micronutrient deficiencies, antibiotic use, cesarean delivery, beta-1,3/1,6-glucan immunomodulation, and short-chain fatty acids in autism spectrum disorders. Although poor sanitation and water quality are mentioned briefly as background context for enteric pathogen exposure in the MAL-ED cohort overview, the record does not study household or community water/sanitation service access (C1), any legal, administrative, or governance mechanism (C2), or any water/sanitation service access outcome (C4). Excluded under E01 (wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the plain institutional/governance reading yield exclusion: this biomedical symposium compilation examines gut microbiota, nutrition, antibiotic exposure, cesarean delivery, beta-glucan immunology, and autism spectrum disorders, with zero legal, administrative, regulatory, or governance mechanisms and no water or sanitation access outcomes.

evidence_quotes.quote: GUT in FOCUS Symposium NOBEL FORUM, Karolinska Institutet, February 2nd 2015

The Etiology, Risk Factors and Interactions of Enteric Infections and Malnutrition and the Consequences for Child Health and Development Project (MAL-ED) was started in 2009 to investigate the role of enteric infections, nutritional intake, and other environmental exposure variables on child development.
NoMIC is a prospective birth cohort established for the purpose of studying the colonization of infant gut microbiota and subsequent health
